newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - June 27.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - June 27.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Friday :

* U.S. stocks fell on Thursday on investor concern over corporate earnings and rising long-term interest rates ahead of a meeting of Federal Reserve policy makers next week. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 35.73 points to close at 7,654.25.
* OPEC talks in Vienna resulted in an agreement to try to rescue weak oil prices by extending a freeze on the cartel's production quotas until the end of the year.
* On Thursday, the Jakarta Composite Index closed down 3.09 at 709.41 points. Brokers said the index was pulled down by selling in blue chip stocks led by a sharp fall in Telkom .
* On Friday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,430.40/31.40 at 0155 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,430.00/32.75.
* Blue chip toll-road operator Citra Marga Nusaphala Persada and transportation firm Steady Safe after Steady Safe reportedly said it will buy an 11.01 percent stake in Citra Marga.

* Cigarette stocks Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna ahead of its annual shareholders' meeting on Friday coupled with market talk of a possible swap of shares between HM Sampoerna's founder, Putera Sampoerna, and a major shareholder of the Salim group conglomerate. Both groups have stakes in noodle maker Indofood and Astra International.

* Property firm Bakrieland Development on market talk of possible acquisitions after an executive of its holding company, PT Bakrie Capital Indonesia, told Reuters on Thursday the proceeds of its planned rights issue will be used to finance some acquisitions. No details of the rights issue were available.
* Timber firm Daya Sakti on company expectations that it will post a 1997 net profit at 18 billion rupiah against 9.0 billion rupiah in 1996.
* Energy firm PT Medco Energy after Bisnis Indonesia newspaper reported the firm had provided $60 million to take a stake in Britain's Dragon Oil.
* Engineering firm Bukaka Teknik Utama after president director Fadel Muhammad reportedly indicated the firm was considering strategic alliances with foreign firms. He gave no details.

* Property firm PT Jakarta International Hotel Development (JIHD) on reports that it will increase its stake in cellular phone operator Satelindo to 25 percent from the current 21.37 percent. Also on a report in Bisnis Indonesia on Friday that Satelindo planned to sell 10 percent of its shares to the public by the end of 1997.
